status_summary: No proposed or final rule amending the child labor hazardous occupations orders was found since 2025-01-20. The Federal Register search of Labor Department documents for child labor returned only a joint employer proposal (2026-04-23) and a proposal on removing non-notice-and-comment interpretive provisions (2025-07-02). A trade-press report of the Wage and Hour Division head's March 2026 remarks described a priority on enforcement against the worst forms of child labor, including minors in dangerous jobs, and the division's 2026 regulatory agenda as published 2026-07-06 listed a joint employer proposal and an independent contractor rule, not child labor.
title: Amend child labor hazard orders so teens can do regulated jobs with training and consent
uncertainties: This is an absence-of-evidence finding. Checks run: Federal Register API queries on child labor (Labor Department) by the researcher and, in review, on hazardous occupations, youth employment and minors for the Wage and Hour Division since 2025-01-20 (no documents); four WebSearches in all (three by the researcher, one in review on teen hazardous-occupation proposals, which returned only 2018 coverage); fetches of the two trade-press articles. The Unified Agenda database at reginfo.gov could not be searched, so an agenda entry might exist that was not seen. A first-term proposal on 16 and 17 year old hazardous work was reported in 2018 by a safety trade publication; it predates the window and is not counted.
